messages:
mari_peopleops: Thanks everyone — posting a quick follow-up thread from today’s all‑hands. If you have any remaining questions about reviews, leveling, promotions, comp timing, or benefits, drop them here and we’ll get answers from the relevant folks. Recording + slides: <https://redwood.example/allhands/rec>

sam_peopleops: Quick note — we will publish the calibration guidance doc later today with the final timelines.

dave_eng: Question about calibration exceptions: my manager updated my rating after the calibration meeting due to a missing project note. Will that change how comp is calculated or trigger a retro pay process? cc @mari_peopleops

mari_peopleops: Short answer: if a manager submits a documented correction before the cutoff for compensation inputs, it will be included in the comp cycle. If the change comes after the comp input cutoff, we evaluate for retroactive adjustments via an exceptions review. Please email exceptions@redwood.com with the manager note and timestamp.

jess_hrbp: To add — managers should attach their calibration notes in the manager portal. If there’s a dispute about evidence, open a thread with your HRBP and include the examples; we’ll handle on a case-by-case basis. :sparkles:

tanya_pm: For promotions — what’s the effective date? If someone is promoted during a review, does the new base go into payroll immediately or the next cycle?

ben_finance: We process approved comp changes in the next payroll cycle after approvals clear. Retroactive pay (if applicable) is paid via an off-cycle payment targeted for the end of the following month. Example: approve on 2026-03-05 -> base updated on next cycle, retro paid 2026-03-31 off-cycle. If you need exact dates for your org, ping me.

elena_ceo: Also want to reiterate: promotions should come with a clear role and impact summary. If managers need help writing that summary I’m happy to review samples — DM me and I’ll jump in for coaching. Thanks for flagging the edge cases.

dave_eng: Follow-up — equity refresh eligibility for ICs who get promoted to Sr within the cycle? Any hard rule?

mari_peopleops: There’s no strict automatic refresh on promotion. Typically refresh nominations happen during comp cycle reviews and managers nominate based on level, impact, and time since last grant. Rule of thumb: eligible for consideration after 6–12 months depending on previously granted equity and role change. Your manager + HRBP can push a nomination if warranted.

alex_benefits: BOT: Parental leave policy unchanged — primary caregiver: up to 16 weeks paid; secondary caregiver: up to 8 weeks paid. Policy doc: <https://redwood.example/policies/parental-leave>. For case-specific questions, benefits@redwood.com.

mari_peopleops: Great thread — I’ll compile these into a mini‑FAQ and post it in #people-ops later today. We’ll also schedule office hours next week for any live clarifications. Thanks all! :raised_hands:
